claims.text: The dynamic behavior of solidified FeNiCrMn across temperature and strain-rate regimes is governed by adiabatic shear-band formation.
Adiabatic shear-band formation enhances the penetration properties of FeNiCrMn.
High strain rates promote the formation of adiabatic shear bands.
Adiabatic shear bands arise from strongly localized deformation.
The proposed mechanism applies from -200°C to 500°C.
The proposed mechanism applies over strain rates from 10^-3 s^-1 to 10^3 s^-1.
Quasi-static mechanical properties of FeNiCrMn provide the baseline for comparison.
The relationship between adiabatic shear bands and penetration properties is not well understood.
The hypothesis can be tested by compression testing solidified FeNiCrMn at varied temperatures and strain rates.
Yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, ductility, and microstructure will be measured in the proposed experiment.
Failure of adiabatic shear bands to enhance penetration properties would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis assigns adiabatic shear bands a governing role across the entire stated strain-rate range, including 10^-3 s^-1, while the mechanism specifically attributes their formation to high strain rates and localized deformation.
The design specifies compression testing but lists ultimate tensile strength as a measurement, which is not ordinarily obtained from a compression test.

The predicted and falsifying outcome concerns penetration properties, but the experiment includes no penetration or ballistic-performance measurement, so the stated falsification rule cannot be applied directly.
